note: Root matrix for Happy Flops. Sub-worlds (submundos) inherit from this and may override free_variables only. Invariants are immutable at every layer.

brand.name: Happy Flops
brand.definition: A brand built around comfort, simplicity and everyday happiness, that makes ordinary moments feel better.
brand.origin_story: Standing for hours settling his daughter to sleep, his feet genuinely hurt. A different sandal removed the pain entirely. 'Why doesn't everyone feel this?' became the brand.
brand.promise: Comfort is not a luxury. Happiness shouldn't be complicated.
differentiate_from: generic cloud-slide brands (product floating on flat white, no brand world)
orthopaedic and clinical brands (arch diagrams, pharmacy aesthetic)
sneaker and hype brands (hard backdrops, aggressive studio light)
low-cost pool-slide brands (stacked product, garish colour on flat ground)
visual_references: Pammys (NOTE: direct competitor, same category and market — use knowingly)

positioning_evolution.from: Brand Book V1: 'Happy Flops lives in real life - always.'
positioning_evolution.to: A brand that lives between life and imagination.
positioning_evolution.why_it_matters: The original line made every non-photographic world an awkward exception. This makes flat colour backgrounds, creative photoshoots, 3D and the character universe legitimate territory rather than concessions. The Brand Book calls itself a living document; this is recorded as a declared evolution, not a violation.
positioning_evolution.consequence: The 'real life always' principle governs the Exterior and Casa worlds. It does not govern Creative Photoshoot, Characters or the 3D track.

smiletech.name: SmileTech
smiletech.what_it_is: The flex. Happy Flops bend with the foot instead of staying rigid like most slides on the market.
smiletech.why_the_name: The smile in the logo, the curve the sole makes when it bends, and the name are the same shape. The Brand Book already describes the logo's smile as a 'flexible curve' reflecting the softness of the sandals.
smiletech.replaces: any mention of EVA foam or material engineering in customer-facing communication
smiletech.internal_material_fact: EVA foam (do not say this publicly)
how_to_talk_about_it: Say what it does, never how it works
Show the bend, don't diagram it
Feeling first: 'it moves with you', not 'flexible polymer construction'
smiletech.visual_signature: the bend — the sole curving as the foot rolls, held in hand, flexed between two fingers, mid-step
smiletech.status: new — does not yet exist in any brand asset

voice.core_rule: Speak simply, clearly, positively. Don't over-explain. Don't try too hard. Let the feeling speak.
canonical_examples: Soft enough to forget the day
Cold outside, warm on your feet

claims_policy.allowed: comfort, cushioning, softness, relief from tiredness, ease

happy_not_happy.description: Binary contrast device. Happy = this, Not Happy = the rigid slide you've always worn.
happy_not_happy.note: Scoped deliberately. Used everywhere it stops being a device and becomes a tic.

invariants.name: light
invariants.rule: Light is soft and directional — never flat, never harsh, never flash. The source is always readable. Colour temperature follows the scene and season; softness and direction never change.

invariants.name: colour_richness
invariants.rule: Colour is rich but credible — clearly more beautiful than reality, but still believable. A working target is roughly +10-15% saturation, but this is a heuristic judged by eye, NOT a measured specification. Do not treat the number as gospel. Never grey, dull, desaturated or fake-HDR.

invariants.name: colour_structure_environment
invariants.rule: The ENVIRONMENT resolves to ONE dominant tone and ONE accent, graded warm. This governs the room, the background and the styling — NOT the product. The product may carry any number of colours: Leopard, Pineapple, Pizza, White Marble and the six Botanics designs are multicolour by design. A quiet environment is precisely what makes a loud product read.

invariants.name: feet
invariants.rule: Feet must never distract from the product. Clean, natural, minimal, toes relaxed and close together. If the toes become the focal point, the image is wrong.

invariants.name: no_generated_text
invariants.rule: No lettering, logos, watermarks or signage inside the image, ever. Type is set afterwards. The store publishes in 20 languages — one clean image serves all of them.

invariants.name: product_fidelity
invariants.rule: The product matches the approved reference pack. Never described-and-hoped.

invariants.name: casting
invariants.rule: WHEN PEOPLE APPEAR they are real, unposed, multigenerational and diverse. Scandinavian and European environments; the Nordic idea lives in place, architecture and light, not in people. Images with no people in them are not a violation of this rule.

invariants.name: forbidden_scenes
invariants.rule: No gym, workplace, clinical settings, cold or stressful situations.

invariants.name: no_third_party_ip
invariants.rule: No third-party or licensed characters, mascots or IP. Happy Flops' OWN characters (Happy Universe Characters) are permitted and have their own world.

invariants.name: typography
invariants.rule: Sniglet and Helvetica only. Sniglet Extra Bold uppercase for H1, Sniglet Regular lowercase for H2, Helvetica Regular sentence case for body.

invariants.name: hands
invariants.rule: Hands are anatomically correct and unremarkable: five fingers, natural pose, short clean nails, no polish, no jewellery, no strain. Hands never become the subject. This matters as much as the feet rule — hands are the second most common anatomical failure in image models, and the signature SmileTech shot (the sole flexed between two fingers) is a hands shot.

moment.description: What is actually happening — a real thing people do

format.description: Any aspect ratio, decided per project

composition.description: Free — leave clean negative space for type

camera.description: Lens, angle, distance, depth — all free

energy.description: From quiet warmth to full movement

styling.description: Any, provided it never competes with the product

seasons.spring: High clear fresh light. Neutral daylight warmed in the highlights. Sun through new leaves, morning to mid-morning. Greens allowed to be vivid.
seasons.summer: Classic golden hour. Low warm sun, long shadows, honeyed glow.
seasons.autumn: Low amber sun lasting all afternoon. Hazy backlight, rim light through leaves, rust and ochre ground tones.
seasons.winter_outdoor: Crisp low winter sun, pale gold, long shadows. Cool air, warm highlights. Never flat grey.
seasons.winter_indoor: Warm lamplight and low window light at dusk. The world of HappyCozy, Fluffs and Comfy.

colour_system.held_together_by: invariant 3 — one dominant, one accent, graded warm

branding.intent: Emotion carries the frame. The product is present and worn, but not the hero.

brand_to_sell.intent: The product is the hero, held inside a real emotional moment. Both must read in one second.

product_sell.intent: The product is the absolute hero. Clear, direct, fast. No ambiguity, no storytelling.

prompt_blocks.invariant_block: Light is soft and directional — never flat, never harsh, never flash. The source is always readable. Colour is rich but credible: about 10-15% more saturated than reality, still possible as a photograph. The frame resolves to ONE dominant tone and ONE accent, graded warm. People are real, unposed, caught mid-movement — multigenerational and diverse. Styling is simple and comfortable and never competes with the product. Feet are clean and well-groomed, natural skin, toes relaxed and close together, soft natural position, bare neutral nails. Feet stay secondary — the product is where the eye lands. Hands, where visible, are anatomically correct and unremarkable — five fingers, natural relaxed pose, short clean bare nails, no jewellery. The product matches the reference image exactly. Feeling over perfection: warm, alive, slightly imperfect.
prompt_blocks.negative_prompt: extra toes, missing toes, six toes, fused toes, merged toes, splayed toes, curled toes, gripping toes, tense toes, deformed feet, malformed foot anatomy, extreme toe close-up, dirty feet, cracked skin, dry skin, calluses, long toenails, coloured nail polish, veiny feet, text, lettering, words, logo, watermark, signage, captions, gym, fitness equipment, office, desk, workplace, hospital, clinical setting, cold atmosphere, stress, white sky, blown-out sky, grey, desaturated, dull, cold colour cast, heavy filter, HDR, oversaturated, harsh flash, direct flash, flat overhead lighting, hard shadows, no visible light direction, professional model, catalog pose, stiff posing, plastic skin, over-retouched, airbrushed, cluttered background, messy room, empty studio void, third-party characters, licensed characters, competitor branding, extra fingers, missing fingers, six fingers, fused fingers, deformed hands, malformed hand anatomy, twisted wrist, claw hand, nail polish on hands, rings, bracelets, watch, long fingernails

submundo_rule: A submundo may override free_variables only. It may never add to, weaken or contradict an invariant.

tooling.higgsfield: lifestyle scenes with people and movement — branding and brand_to_sell
tooling.nano_banana: Gemini 2.5 Flash Image — product accuracy, colourway swaps, repairing product drift. Reference conditioning is far stronger.
tooling.critical_rule: Never describe the product and hope. Always attach the reference image.

Hex or Pantone per colourway. 'Bordeaux Red' is not an instruction — ask ten people for red and you get ten reds, and the AI is those ten people every time. Colour error is the one failure on this list that costs money directly: a customer who receives a different burgundy than the photo returns it.

styling_doctrine.rule_unchanged: Styling is simple, comfortable, effortless and never competes with the product. This rule is NOT changed.
styling_doctrine.clarification: 'Never competes' does not mean 'never noticeable'. Competes = the eye lands on the clothes first, or cannot decide. Noticeable = the clothes are good, styled and current, and the product is still the first thing you see. A stylist's job is to choose the look that makes the product read BETTER — good styling makes a product pop, it does not hide it.

practice.colour: The outfit sits in a register that lets the product's colourway separate from it. Beige product against beige trousers disappears — a styling failure, not a photography one.
practice.pattern: Never near the product. Pattern above the waist is fine; pattern on trousers, socks or floor is not.
practice.silhouette: Hems reveal the foot cleanly. Long trousers that swallow the product defeat the shot.
practice.ads: Product hero, outfit as frame. Should catch the eye and look good while the product stays unmistakably the subject.

styling_doctrine.test: Cover the product with your thumb. If the image is still just as good, the product was never the hero.
styling_doctrine.note: Raised as a possible root conflict by the Outfits world and resolved inside the free variables without a Matrix Feedback row — which is what the protocol says to check first.

dna.note: Corrected 20 Aug 2026. Light, colour and feeling are ROOT — brand DNA. They are not collectible variables and no world or collection chooses them.
dna.the_sequence: The ROOT SAYS what the light, the colour and the feeling are. The TRUNK SHOWS what that looks like. The WORLD says where it happens.
dna.light: Invariant 1. Always soft, always directional, always warm-graded relative to its own scene. Winter, Christmas, summer — the light is always THAT light. Only colour temperature follows the scene.
dna.colour: Invariants 2 and 3. Rich but credible; environment resolves to one dominant and one accent.
dna.feeling: The brand thesis — we sell moments, not sandals. Everyday Joy is a pillar, not a collection.
dna.consequence: A trunk collection is EVIDENCE, not choice. A light reference with hard flat light is not another kind of light in the library — it is a REJECTED reference, because it breaks invariant 1. Every trunk reference names the invariant it illustrates and carries a verdict: exemplar or rejected.

tree.note: From Laura's drawing (20 Aug) and the three-category simplification that followed. Six levels.

levels.name: RAIZ — la matriz
levels.is: The 100 questions and the 11 invariants. Brand DNA.

levels.name: TRONCO — referencias de la matriz
levels.is: Evidence of the DNA: luz, felicidad, poses, modelos, imperfecciones, material.

levels.name: CATEGORIA
levels.changeable: rarely — these are the positioning itself

levels.name: SUBCATEGORIA
levels.is: The variation inside a category, including season.

sap_flows_both_ways.up: Root → trunk → category → content type → leaf. This is the normal direction and it is strong.
sap_flows_both_ways.down: The trunk can move the ROOT a little. When references consistently show something the matrix hasn't captured, the DNA can sharpen — never contradict itself, only get more precise. Weighted, not symmetric: a lot flows up, a little flows down.
sap_flows_both_ways.governance: Downward flow still goes through Matrix Feedback and Laura decides. The can_nudge_root flag marks it; it does not authorise it.

what_this_replaced.campaign_layer: Removed. What was called a campaign is a TIPO DE CONTENIDO. campana.producto becomes tipo.fotografia_producto.
what_this_replaced.3d_sibling_root: Removed. 3D Render is a CATEGORY. This eliminates the two-roots-drifting risk that the sibling-root design carried.

categories.note: Three. They are not an arbitrary grouping — they ARE the positioning. Lifestyle is life. Render_3D is imagination. Photoshoot is the bridge between them. 'A brand that lives between life and imagination' stops being a slogan and becomes the index of the system.

lifestyle.is: Real life, real people, real places.

exterior.note: Street, city, nature, beach. Absorbs what was previously the separate Naturaleza category.

interior.note: Home. Winter interior is where HappyCozy, Fluffs and Comfy live.

lifestyle.references: Each subcategory carries its own season references.

photoshoot.is: Controlled shooting. Flat colour or gradient, studio light. Product-led and content-led.
photoshoot.note: Subcategories here are occasions and themes rather than places. The only calendar-independent category, which is why it can produce all year.
photoshoot.references: Its own — more product, more content.

render_3d.note: The 3D characters LIVE WITH REALITY — this is not a separate visual universe sealed off from the brand. Characters and real environments coexist in frame.
render_3d.references: 3D references, including how rendered and real sit together.

version_note: Bumps to 1.0.0 when the first real references land. Tying 1.0 to evidence rather than to how settled the structure feels.
trunk_change: No structural change. Imperfecciones simply gets its own reference collection like the others.

content_types.note: A content type is an ASSIGNMENT, not a place. It runs under a category — the same content type can run under more than one.

registry.note: Model looks for social. Resolved 20 Aug: outfits are shot INSIDE photoshoot or INSIDE lifestyle, so it is an assignment rather than a location. Its styling doctrine already exists and carries over unchanged.
